Blocks.Text: As a LinkedIn partner, you must delete your customers' data from LinkedIn when they delete the corresponding records in your ATS. Use the Middleware Platform DELETE APIs to remove the data and all its copies. Module 5 covers candidates, applications, job requisitions, and related records, including notes, stages, interview feedback, and attachments. It also verifies that deleted data no longer appears in the Enhanced In-ATS Indicator. To complete Module 5 certification, demonstrate each applicable test case below to LinkedIn.
All test cases in this module use the functional check type. For the rule ID scheme, how to read each test case, and the check type definitions, refer to the certification overview.
In Module 5, the test cases are grouped by purpose:

Candidate deletions: RSC-501-001 and RSC-501-002.
Application deletions: RSC-502-001 and RSC-502-002.
Job requisition and job requisition stage deletions: RSC-504-001, RSC-504-002, and RSC-505-001.
Cross-cutting deletion requirements: RSC-503-001 (versioned APIs), RSC-503-002 (deletion identifier mapping), and RSC-503-003 (deletion confirmation and idempotency).

All DELETE APIs are governed by OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials using your customer application's client ID and secret and support query tunneling (X-HTTP-Method-Override: DELETE). Candidate and application deletions return HTTP 200 with per-entity 204 statuses in the response body. Job requisition, job requisition stage, and attachment deletions return HTTP 204 with per-entity 204 statuses in the response body. Upon success, all copies of the data are deleted.
Rule IDs were renumbered to make each test case unambiguous to reference. Use the following table to map the rule IDs used in earlier revisions of this page to the current ones.

Rows.Text: Delete candidate-related entities1. On an existing candidate that has notes, delete the note(s): DELETE rest/candidateNotes with externalCandidateId, integrationContext, externalNoteId.2. Confirm the note is gone from the Enhanced In-ATS Indicator.3. Then delete the candidate: DELETE rest/candidates with externalCandidateId, integrationContext.4. Confirm the Enhanced In-ATS Indicator for that candidate is gone.

• After deleting the candidate note(s), they are removed from the Enhanced In-ATS Indicator.• After deleting the candidate, the Enhanced In-ATS Indicator for that candidate is removed.• Each delete returns a per-entity 204, and upon success all copies of the data are deleted.Related documentation: Delete candidate notes, delete candidates

Delete an entire candidate1. Delete an existing candidate: DELETE rest/candidates with externalCandidateId, integrationContext.2. Confirm the response returns HTTP 200, and read the per-entity 204 status from the body for the candidate.3. Confirm the Enhanced In-ATS Indicator for that candidate is no longer shown.

• The candidate is deleted from LinkedIn and the Enhanced In-ATS Indicator for that candidate is removed.• Upon success, all copies of the candidate data are deleted.Related documentation: Delete candidates

Delete application-related entities1. On an existing application, delete its note(s): DELETE rest/applicationNotes with externalJobApplicationId, integrationContext, externalNoteId; confirm gone from the indicator.2. Delete its stage(s): DELETE rest/applicationStage with jobApplicationId, jobApplicationStageId, integrationContext; confirm gone.3. Delete its interview feedback: DELETE rest/applicationInterviewFeedbacks with jobApplicationId, interviewFeedbackId, integrationContext; confirm gone.4. Delete any resume attachment: DELETE rest/attachments with externalReferenceEntityId, externalAttachmentId, integrationContext, externalReferenceEntityType=APPLICATION, attachmentType=RESUME.

• After deleting each related entity (notes, stages, interview feedback, attachments), it is removed from the Enhanced In-ATS Indicator.• Each delete returns a per-entity 204, and upon success all copies of the data are deleted.Related documentation: Delete application notes, delete application stages, delete application interview feedback, delete attachments

Delete an entire application1. Delete an existing application: DELETE rest/applications with atsJobApplicationId, integrationContext.2. Confirm the response returns HTTP 200, and read the per-entity 204 status from the body for the application.3. Confirm the Enhanced In-ATS Indicator for that application is no longer shown.

• The application is deleted from LinkedIn and the Enhanced In-ATS Indicator for that application is removed.• Upon success, all copies of the application data are deleted.Related documentation: Delete applications

Blocks.Text: These test cases apply across all deletions in Module 5.

Rows.Text: Demonstrate support for versioned APIs1. Explain or demonstrate that your integration uses the versioned rest/ DELETE endpoints with the LinkedIn-Version header (set to a currently supported API version) rather than the deprecated unversioned or /v2 endpoints.2. Confirm the plan and status for migrating any remaining unversioned calls.

• The partner uses (or has a concrete plan to migrate to) the versioned rest/ DELETE APIs with the correct LinkedIn-Version header.• This is the same versioning requirement tracked in Module 6 (RSC-601-001).Related documentation: API versioning

Map deletion identifiers (certification prerequisite)1. Produce a mapping of each deletable entity → its DELETE endpoint and required identifiers: candidate (externalCandidateId), candidate note (+ externalNoteId), application (atsJobApplicationId), application note (externalJobApplicationId + externalNoteId), application stage (jobApplicationId + jobApplicationStageId), interview feedback (jobApplicationId + interviewFeedbackId), job requisition (externalJobRequisitionId), job requisition stage (+ jobRequisitionStageId), attachment (externalReferenceEntityId + externalAttachmentId + externalReferenceEntityType + attachmentType), each with integrationContext (and dataProvider=ATS on legacy /v2 endpoints).2. Confirm the identifiers reuse the same external IDs you synced in Module 2 (strict 1:1).

• Share a mapping between each deletable entity and its DELETE endpoint and required identifiers, reusing the identical external IDs synced in Module 2.• This mapping is a certification prerequisite used for the LinkedIn testing and verification (code review).

Confirm deletions and verify idempotency1. On any delete, inspect the response body and confirm the per-entity 204 status (and check for error statuses on individual entities).2. Re-issue the same delete for an already-deleted entity and confirm it is handled safely (no error surfaced to the customer).

• The partner checks the per-entity status in each DELETE response and handles errors for individual entities.• Re-deleting an already-deleted entity is safe, and upon success all copies of the data are deleted.

Delete job requisition-related entities1. On an existing requisition that has stages, delete the stage(s): DELETE rest/jobRequisitionStages with externalJobRequisitionId, jobRequisitionStageId, integrationContext.2. Confirm the stage is gone from the stage dropdown in the associated ATS Connected Project.3. Then delete the requisition: DELETE rest/jobRequisitions with externalJobRequisitionId, integrationContext.4. Confirm the requisition is no longer available in One Click Export or Connected Projects.

• After deleting the stage(s), they no longer appear for that requisition.• After deleting the requisition, it is removed from LinkedIn (One Click Export dropdown and any Connected Project).• Each delete returns a per-entity 204, and upon success all copies of the data are deleted.Related documentation: Delete job requisition stages, delete job requisitions

Delete an entire job requisition1. Delete an existing requisition: DELETE rest/jobRequisitions with externalJobRequisitionId, integrationContext.2. Confirm the response returns HTTP 204, and read the per-entity 204 status from the body for the requisition.3. Confirm the requisition no longer appears in One Click Export or Connected Projects.

• The requisition is deleted from LinkedIn and is no longer selectable in One Click Export or Connected Projects.• Upon success, all copies of the requisition data are deleted.Related documentation: Delete job requisitions

Delete a job requisition stage1. Delete an existing stage: DELETE rest/jobRequisitionStages with externalJobRequisitionId, jobRequisitionStageId, integrationContext.2. Confirm the response returns HTTP 204, and read the per-entity 204 status from the body for the stage.3. Confirm the stage no longer appears in the stage dropdown for Applicants in the associated ATS Connected Project.
• The stage is deleted from LinkedIn and no longer appears for that requisition.• Upon success, all copies of the stage data are deleted.Related documentation: Delete job requisition stages
